attempts.why: Pelipper's Drizzle was up before the first action, which halved every Fire attack in a Fire room and turned Mega Swampert into a Swift Swim sweeper. Turn 1 Mega Swampert's Liquidation broke Infernape's Focus Sash while Ariados laid Sticky Web and Infernape's Fake Out flinched Pelipper. Turn 2 Rage Powder pulled Liquidation off Infernape and Hurricane (no-miss in rain, 2x into Bug) removed Ariados. Turn 3 the grunt withdrew the 1 HP Infernape for Nidoking, which died to a rain-boosted Liquidation in one action, and Magmortar's Thunderbolt - 4x into Water/Flying - removed Pelipper outright. Turn 4 Infernape came back, Fake Out flinched Mega Swampert, Urshifu's Aqua Jet finished Infernape and Magmortar's Thunderbolt then removed Urshifu at full HP (2x into Water/Fighting). Landorus came in Ground-immune to the Thunderbolt and Liquidation closed it out.

strategy_checks.evidence: Sticky Web on turn 1, Rage Powder on turn 2. The plan's sentence says Ariados 'does not do both'; in play the AI fitted both in before it died, which is the better line, not a defect. The web was not cosmetic - it dropped Urshifu's Speed a stage on its turn-3 switch-in, which is visible in the turn-4 state.

strategy_checks.check: Rage Powder redirects a single-target attack aimed at the partner
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2: Mega Swampert's Liquidation was submitted at battler 3 (Infernape, sitting on 1 HP after the Focus Sash) and resolved into battler 1 (Ariados) for 30 - the damage dict credits slot 1, not slot 3, and Infernape stayed at exactly 1 HP. The redirection is mechanically live and it did its job: it denied the kill on Infernape for a turn.
I never aimed Spore at it - Amoonguss was never deployed in a four-turn fight - so the ability is correctly authored but untested here.

strategy_checks.check: Infernape uses Fake Out only when the bought turn beats immediate damage
strategy_checks.evidence: Two Fake Outs, both with real payoff. Turn 1 it flinched Pelipper, which denied the Hydro Pump that would have broken the Focus Sash a turn early. Turn 4, on re-entry at 1 HP, it flinched Mega Swampert - that denied 22 damage to Magmortar and, more importantly, kept Magmortar alive to fire the Thunderbolt that KOed Urshifu. That second Fake Out is the better of the two and it was made from a 1 HP body that was going to die anyway. Good use of a dying turn.

strategy_checks.check: Magmortar behind redirection is the room's damage, with Heat Wave into both slots
strategy_checks.result: FAIL as written, PASS as AI judgment
strategy_checks.evidence: Magmortar never used Heat Wave. It used Thunderbolt on turns 3 and 4 and killed a full-HP Pelipper (4x) and a full-HP Urshifu (2x) with it. That is exactly right: Drizzle was up, which halves Fire, and both of my actives were Water. The authored line is a plan written for a board that did not occur, and the AI correctly abandoned it. Recording it as a plan FAIL rather than an AI FAIL - the dossier's 'Heat Wave into both slots' sentence should be read as conditional.

protect_summary: 0 opponent Protects across 4 turns and 7 decisions, from a team with three Protect users. No empty guards, no repetition. The room simply never had a turn where Protect beat attacking, and the AI agreed.
ai_notes: Turn 3's withdrawal of the 1 HP Infernape looked at first like a bad switch - it put a 2x-Water-weak Nidoking into a slot facing a Mega Swampert that had used Liquidation on each of the previous two turns under its own rain. It is not a defect: Nidoking was the only reserve left, and preserving a 1 HP Infernape that would die to anything in order to land a second Fake Out later is a correct trade, which it then actually cashed on turn 4. Recording it as a good decision that looked bad.
Target selection was excellent throughout. Magmortar picked Thunderbolt over its STAB into two Water bodies under rain, twice, and both times it was a clean KO from full HP.
AI decision budget: max 57 frames (0.954 s), inside the 1.2 s budget.
level_change_rationale: Keep. Won on the first attempt but it cost Pelipper and Urshifu outright - two faints, which is the dossier's 'real fight' band, and both faints were full-HP one-shots rather than chip. The rule text for +1 requires 0-1 faints and no real threat; this was neither. Offsets stay at 0 on all four.
cooler: Yes, and the dossier already half-admits it. The room's stated signature is the Rage Powder dilemma, but the member that actually threatened me was Magmortar, whose Life Orb Thunderbolt one-shot two of my six from full health - and Thunderbolt is the one move on this team the plan never mentions. Two honest observations rather than changes: (1) the Rage Powder question is much weaker than authored against any Grass-typed or airborne lead, and my party happened to hold both answers (Amoonguss, Pelipper) without trying, so the dilemma is closer to a tax than a puzzle; (2) Nidoking is the weak link in practice, not on paper - it is the only member with no interaction with either Ariados's redirection or the Fire pair's pressure, and it will usually arrive last into a board that has already resolved. If this room is ever revisited, the interesting version is Nidoking with a redirection payoff (something that wants a free turn) rather than a fourth independent attacker. No change made in this pass.
